hero.alt: Dark green illustration with the title Does Discharge Break Wudu

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 303a, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Ali asked about madhi; the Prophet said to wash the private part and perform ablution.

sources.title: Mazur With Regular Discharge, Darul Ifta Birmingham (fatwa 05401)
sources.supports: Defines madhi, wadi and mani; madhi and wadi require wudu, mani requires ghusl; advice on waswas.

sources.title: Discharging of Madhi, Darul Ifta Birmingham (fatwa 02182)
sources.supports: Clear sticky discharge is madhi; it breaks wudu but does not require ghusl; soiled clothing is washed.

sources.title: Does Vaginal Discharge Break the Wudhu, Darul Ifta Birmingham (fatwa 04148)
sources.supports: Normal clear rutubat al-farj is pure and does not break wudu; pad guidance; continuous discharge makes one excused with wudu per fard prayer time.

sources.title: Les secretions vaginales annulent-elles les ablutions, Dar al-Ifta al-Misriyyah (fatwa 13044)
sources.supports: Irregular vaginal secretions break wudu without requiring ghusl; constant secretions are treated like incontinence with wudu per prayer.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 228, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Woman with persistent non-menstrual bleeding told to keep praying and perform ablution for every prayer.

sources.title: Does Discharge Break the Wudhu?, Darul Ifta Birmingham (fatwa 03313)
sources.supports: Being excused for habitual discharge does not extend to madhi, which still requires wudu.

sources.title: Wudu and madhi, Darul Ifta Birmingham (fatwa 02268)
sources.supports: Madhi requires washing and repeating wudu; advises tissue in the undergarment and seeing a doctor if it persists.

sources.title: Vaginal discharge, NHS
sources.supports: Describes normal discharge and changes in colour, smell or texture that warrant medical advice.

review.notes: Read each retrieved page text this run: Muslim 303a, Bukhari 228, Darul Ifta Birmingham fatwas 04148, 03313, 05401, 02182, 02268, Dar al-Ifta Egypt fatwa 13044 (French original, paraphrased not quoted) and NHS vaginal discharge page. Both sides of the vaginal discharge disagreement are attributed to named institutions; no universal fatwa given. Bukhari 178 returned 403 and was not used. Hero inspected: 1200x630 title card.

claim_checks.claim: Madhi requires washing and ablution, not ghusl
claim_checks.explanation: Hadith says he should wash his organ and perform ablution, with no bath mentioned.

claim_checks.claim: Madhi and wadi require wudu and mani requires ghusl
claim_checks.explanation: Fatwa 05401 lists the three fluids with exactly these rulings.

claim_checks.claim: Clear sticky discharge is madhi, breaks wudu, no ghusl
claim_checks.explanation: Fatwa 02182 states this directly and says soiled portions are washed.

claim_checks.claim: Normal clear vaginal wetness is pure and does not break wudu per this fatwa
claim_checks.explanation: Fatwa 04148 calls it rutubat al-farj, deems it pure and says wudu will not break, citing Raddul Muhtar.

claim_checks.claim: Excused person makes wudu for each fard prayer valid for that time
claim_checks.explanation: Fatwa 04148 states a Ma'zoor makes wudu for every fardh salah, valid for the salah time.

claim_checks.claim: Egyptian Dar al-Ifta says irregular vaginal secretions break wudu without ghusl
claim_checks.explanation: The French fatwa states such secretions annul ablutions and do not require full washing.

claim_checks.claim: Constant secretions treated like incontinence; wet underwear need not be washed while excuse lasts
claim_checks.explanation: The fatwa states regular constant secretions take the ruling of urinary incontinence and the underwear need not be washed during the excuse.

claim_checks.claim: Prophet told woman with persistent bleeding to perform ablution for every prayer
claim_checks.explanation: Bukhari 228 includes Hisham's father's addition: perform ablution for every prayer.

claim_checks.claim: Excuse for habitual discharge does not cover madhi
claim_checks.explanation: Fatwa 03313 says the same ruling does not apply to madhi and wudu is required.

claim_checks.claim: Advice to use tissue and consult a doctor if discharge persists
claim_checks.explanation: Fatwa 02268 recommends a cloth or tissue and consulting a doctor.

claim_checks.claim: Normal discharge is clear or white; changes may signal infection
claim_checks.explanation: NHS page lists normal characteristics and advises help when colour, smell or texture changes.
